newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts this week - market seen well supported.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts this week - market seen well supported.

text.p: UK gilts will be fairly well underpinned this week but may have trouble keeping up with their European counterparts as potentially strong economic data adds to speculation of a further interest rate rise, analysts said.
"We're off to a fairly good start. The tone for the week looks reasonable," Societe Generale gilts analyst Tom Rayner said.
Gilts reversed early losses on Monday, after the November UK Purchasing Managers' Index showed expansion in the manufacturing sector for the sixth consecutive month.
By 1155 GMT, the gilt/Bund spread was 183 basis points.
Rayner said he expected Thursday's CBI distributive trades survey to confirm the recovery in the UK manufacturing sector.
"German data will also be important. If we see a weakish third quarter GDP number, or if the outlook looks weak for the fourth quarter, I think that again will be positive," he said.
According to a Reuter poll, Germany's gross domestic product, due on Wednesday, is forecast to have grown 1.5 percent year-on-year in the third quarter, versus 1.1 percent in Q2.
Rayner said weak German data could push Bunds higher, while U.S. leading indicators,later Monday, could drive Treasuries up.

"If the European and U.S. markets do well this week, we should end up higher in absolute terms," Rayner said. But he added gilts may struggle to keep up in relative terms, with the gilt/Bund spread heading to 185 bps by the end of the week.
He said the market's ability to fully absorb Wednesday's 2.5 billion stg auction of 7.0 percent gilts due 2002, would also impact on gilts.

Merrill Lynch said the market would carefully watch the UK's October industrial production data, due on Friday. Industrial production is forecast to have grown between 1.2 and 1.9 percent year-on-year versus a 0.3 percent rise in September.

"The official output numbers have, in our opinion, understated the true growth in the manufacturing sector," Merrill Lynch said in its weekly bond report. The market will continue to be dogged by speculation over another interest rate rise ahead of Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's monetary meeting with Bank of England Governor Eddie George on December 11, analysts said.
With signs of inflation re-emerging and consumer spending on the rise, Clarke is under pressure to raise rates from the present 6.0 percent before the election, which must be held by May next year.
Salomon Brothers analyst Michael Saunders said last week's "possibly restrictive" budget could push Britain through a low inflation cycle.

"Fiscal caution raises the odds that the UK can re-run the virtuous circles seen in Italy and Sweden over the past year, namely a strong currency which caps inflation expectations and supports the bond market," Saunders said.

UK retail price and producer price data for November is scheduled to be released next week. Societe Generale's Rayner said sustained overseas demand for gilts would help drive them higher over the week.
"The strength of sterling is obviously underpinning overseas demand," he said. "The Japanese are interested in gilts and the Italians are quite excited about increasing their sterling exposure."
